male.brief: The player's warden, the son, a young Greek warden of a harbour town who keeps its lamps lit through the night, fighting with a xiphos in melee and a bow at range. Greek and heroic, with a readable silhouette that stands out against a dark night: distinct bronze, linen and accent colours, so his armour, cloth and cape do not melt into one colour. Write one call: hero(k, { sex: 'male', melee: 'xiphos', ranged: 'bow', pose: POSE || 'idle', facing: FACING, ...}). The game draws the warden in 20 poses (idle, walk, melee, ranged) from five directions with this same code, so FACING is a global number, in degrees, that the renderer gives your code for each direction: write facing: FACING exactly and never a fixed number. Never pass at, height, build or ready (the game sets them), and call no raw shapes (k.sphere, k.capsule and the others): they would not turn with him. Choose only what makes him look like himself: helmet ('none'|'corinthian'|'attic'), cape, and palette {cloth, accent, hair, skin, metal} with material names from the list.

issues: Armour, pteruges, greaves, skin and bow all render in one warm gold-brown band, so the figure melts into a single colour, which the brief explicitly forbids.
No linen or white cloth is visible: palette.cloth 'marble' does not show on the skirt or chiton, which reads brown.
The crimson accent appears only on the arrow fletching; the cape is not visible from this view, so there is no contrasting accent mass.
The silhouette is otherwise right: xiphos in hand, bow and quiver back-slung, bronze cuirass, greaves and a frontal 3/4 stance.
Armour, pteruges skirt and leg wraps all read as one warm gold-brown mass; no light linen layer is visible, so the colour-separation brief fails.
The cloth:'marble' choice does not show anywhere distinct; the skirt reads brown/bronze, not as a pale linen chiton.
The crimson accent and cape are only a thin sliver behind the bow, so the accent colour barely registers from this direction.
The walk2 legs merge into one gold column and the stride is hard to read at game zoom.
Armour, pteruges skirt, skin and back-slung bow all read as one gold-brown mass; no linen or white cloth is visible anywhere
The cape is almost invisible: only a thin crimson sliver shows behind the shoulder, so the accent colour does not carry the silhouette
The strike reads weakly: the xiphos hangs low and blade-down beside the leg rather than mid-swing, though it is in hand
Bare brown head and brown bow add to the monochrome look against a dark night
Bronze cuirass, skin, wooden bow and greaves are all warm tan/gold and melt into one mass, which the brief explicitly forbids
The marble/linen cloth is barely visible; no white chiton or pteruges read between the armour and legs
The crouched draw pose plus the large bow in front hides the torso silhouette; only the crimson cape gives contrast
The released arrow floats far from the figure and reads as a stray prop

male.rule: every one of four frames is accepted (a verifier pass, or a score of at least 6 with no engine flag) and the mean score beats the deterministic warden's
